Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses BROAD-BASED QRs FOR ADVANCED ICU VENTILATORS GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS 1. The ventilator must be an advanced technology ventilator specifically for use in ICU. 2. It must be capable of ventilating all patient ages, ranging from paediatrics / n eonates / adults. 3. It must be a multi microprocessor-controlled system with individual selection of various ventilation parameters & PEEP. 4. The Ventilator should be USFDA/BIS/Independent Third-party European CE ap proved. The four-digit notified body number must be available if CE is produced. 5. The ventilator must be mounted on a stand with lockable castor wheels. It als o must be supplied with a hinged arm for supporting the breathing circuit. VENTILATION MODES AND CAPABILITIES 1. The ventilator should have the following modes for invasive ventilation: (a) Volume Assist Control, or equivalent. (b) Pressure Assist Control, or equivalent.

(c) Pressure-regulated Volume Control, or equivalent (d) Airway Pressure Release Ventilation, or equivalent (e) Pressure SIMV, with pressure support (f) Volume SIMV, with pressure support (g) Pressure Support Ventilation with selectable volume and pressure mo des for apnea back-up (h) Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Mode. 2. Basic Setting capabilities (a) Tidal Volume 20mL- 1500 mL (b) Flow pattern: square wave and decelerating selection in VCV (c) Mandatory respiratory rate -5-80 breaths per minute (d) Inspiratory time-10 to 80% of breath cycle time (e) Inspiratory plateau 0 to 60% of inspiratory time (f) Rise time-0 to 20% of inspiratory time (g) PEEP 0 to 40 cm H20 (h) PS/PC above PEEP-0 to 50 cm H2O (i) FiO2-21 to 100 % (j) End expiration (% of peak flow) : 1-70 (k) Triggering-Both Flow and Pressure trigger must be available (l) Peak flow :≥ 200 I/min 3. The ventilator should have a dedicated mode for non-invasive ventilation (NI V). The following modes must be available with NIV a. CPAP b. Bi-level positive airway pressure (BiPAP) 4. There must be options for leak compensation and tube resistance compensati on. 5. A reliable and dedicated automated method of PEEP titration and lung protec tive ventilation for ARDS must be available, e.g., Open Lung tool, P/V Pro etc. 6. The I:E ratios must be easily changeable. The ventilator must be capable of d elivering I:E ratios of 1:6- 4:1 or better. 7. It must be capable of both flow and pressure triggering. The flow trigger sensi tivity range must be 0.5 L/min - 10L/min or better. The pressure triggering rang e must be - 10cm H2O- 0cm H2O or better. 8. The cycling threshold in NIV and rise time in invasive ventilation modes must

be user adjustable. It is preferable if the times are actual times/percentages an d not arbitrary levels. 9. The time interval before apnea backup ventilation is triggered (in spontaneou s modes of ventilation like PSV and NIV) must be user-settable. MONITORING AND CONTROL 1. The following must be monitored by the ventilator and displayed as needed. a. Peak airway pressure b. Plateau airway pressure c. Mean airway pressure d. Inspired Tidal Volume e. Expired tidal volume f. Minute Volume g. Static Compliance h. Dynamic Compliance i. Resistance- Inspired and expired j. Respiratory Rate (set) k. Respiratory Rate (total) l. PEEP m. Auto-PEEP n. RSBI o. Work of breathing p. P 0.1 q. Oxygen Inlet Pressure r. Air Inlet Pressure s. FiO2 (measured) t. Delivered FiO2 (set) u. Leak amount v. Time constant w. Elastance 2. It must be capable of performing standard manoeuvres like: a. Inspiratory Hold b. Expiratory Hold c. One-touch increase in FiO2 to 1.0 for suctioning

d. One touch standby and wake-up e. One-touch nebulisation control 3. The ventilator must be capable of: a. Must be able to connect and operate the Aerogen vibrating mesh plate nebuliser with a module built into the ventilator. Each ventilator must be s upplied with two autoclavable Aerogen Pro delivery sets (one installed an d one spare). 4. Oxygen sensors : It is preferable if the ventilator has permanent oxygen sens ors. a. If a disposable oxygen sensor is used, it should be replaced by the com pany during the warranty and CAMC period. 5. Flow sensors: a. For disposable proximal flow sensors, fifty sensors per ventilator must be provided at the time of purchase, and ten sensors per ventilator per ye ar must be provided by the company for the warranty period. b. For reusable distal flow sensors, ten sensors per ventilator must be prov ided at the time of purchase. Five additional sensors per year per ventilato r must be provided by the company throughout the warranty period. 6. The system should have a single-unit reusable, autoclavable expiratory valve/ cassette for complete disinfection. ALARMS 1. The following alarms must be standard. Limits must be user adjustable: a. Airway pressure b. Expired minute volume c. No patient effort (apnea) alarm with automatic return to support mode o n patient triggering d. No consistent patient effort e. Respiratory frequency f. End-expiratory pressure g. High continuous pressure

h. Oxygen Concentration i. Gas supply pressure j. Battery-low charge, low battery voltage k. EtCO2 Limits l. Leakage out of range in NIV m. Technical alarms ( Specific technical faults in internal circuitry) 2. The nature and cause of the alarm must be clearly displayed on the screen. DISPLAY 1. It should be at least 12 inches in size and a TFT/LED touchscreen display. Du al touchscreen and wheel controls are preferable. 2. It must be capable of displaying at least 3 scalars and 2 loops simultaneously for each breath, and a 24-hour trend display of measured parameters. 3. It must preferably display how changing settings influence the breath wavefo rm. 4. The display brightness must be adjustable, and must be readable in bright su nlight. 5. Commonly changed parameters of a breath- The control variable, limit variab le, cycle variable and baseline variable of a breath, Respiratory Rate and FiO2 must be changeable from the home display without using additional menus or o perations. 6. It must have a spill proof and easily cleanable screen display. 7. It should be provided with servo-controlled humidifier with all the accessories ) e.g., Thermostatically servo-controlled humidifier with temperature probe for d igital monitoring of the temperature with alarm facility, reusable heated wire ad apter suitable for disposable/ non-disposable circuit, heating chamber, mountin g brackets, power cord, facility to select active/passive humidification) for smoo th functioning. OTHER SPECIFICATIONS 1. Air source must be turbine/compressor based and quiet (˂50dB). The turbine/ compressor should be from the same manufacturer. The turbine/compressor sh ould have an automatic standby function and must automatically activate on fai lure of the wall air supply. 2. Ventilator battery back-up time must be at least 60 min. 3. Should have facility for ventilation data transfer & network connection. 4. The ventilator must be fully functional even with generic two-limb circuits, an d must not require a particular circuit brand for full functionality. 5. The ventilator must be compatible with the usually available NIV masks and h arnesses.

SUPPLY, DEMONSTRATION, SERVICE AND WARRANTY 1. All the components of the system including turbine/compressor, ventilator tro lley and hinged arm must be from the same manufacturer. The primary manufa cturer must quote directly. 2. The machines must be supplied complete with all the required disposable/spare items (e.g. power cords, patient circuits for both Adult and Pae diatric uses with appropriate masks and connectors, test lung, flow sensors, reu sable humidifier jar, sample tubing with adaptors, user manual etc. in ready to use condition. 3. Technical demonstration of quoted model is must. 4. All reusable and disposable consumables (e.g., power cords, patient circuits f or both Adult and Paediatric uses with appropriate masks and connectors, test l ung, flow sensors, reusable humidifier jar, sample tubing with adaptors, user ma nual etc) being offered should be from the same manufacturer or from a repute d brand with certification of compatibility from the manufacturer, so that warran ty remains intact. 5. Compliance Report must be submitted in a tabulated and point wise manner clearly mentioning the page/paragraph number of original catalogue/literature 6. The manufacturer must have a local authorized service representative. It is p referable if the manufacturer has independent operations in India. 7. The manufacturer must submit user list & performance report within the last 5 years from major hospitals and institutions. 8. A back-to back warranty must be provided by the manufacturer to supply spa res viz power cords, patient circuits for both Adult and Paediatric uses with appr opriate masks and connectors, test lung, flow sensors, reusable humidifier jar, s ample tubing with adaptors for a minimum of 10 years from the date of purchas e. This clause must be independent of the final vendor/ dealer/ channel partner. 9. Consumable / Spare items include a) HEPA Filters b) Oxygen inlet filters c) Du st filter d) Disposable coaxial circuit with flow sensors d) Expiratory membranes e) Oxygen Sensor d) batteries. 10. All reusable components must be covered under warranty and CAMC. 11. The complete list of consumables, their cost, and approximate interval of re placement must be clearly mentioned in writing at the time of bidding. 12. All complaints should be attended to within 24h of reporting and equipment should be restored to full working condition within 5 days even in case of total f ailure of the equipment. 13. Warranty Statement Comprehensive warranty for five years, with an option to enter into CAMC for an additional 5 years. The cost of CAMC must be mention ed in the documents at the time of bidding. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses BROAD-BASED QRs FOR ADVANCED ICU VENTILATORS GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS 1. The ventilator must be an advanced technology ventilator specifically for use in ICU. 2. It must be capable of ventilating all patient ages, ranging from paediatrics / n eonates / adults. 3. It must be a multi microprocessor-controlled system with individual selection of various ventilation parameters & PEEP. 4. The Ventilator should be USFDA/BIS/Independent Third-party European CE ap proved. The four-digit notified body number must be available if CE is produced. 5. The ventilator must be mounted on a stand with lockable castor wheels. It als o must be supplied with a hinged arm for supporting the breathing circuit. VENTILATION MODES AND CAPABILITIES 1. The ventilator should have the following modes for invasive ventilation: (a) Volume Assist Control, or equivalent. (b) Pressure Assist Control, or equivalent.

(c) Pressure-regulated Volume Control, or equivalent (d) Airway Pressure Release Ventilation, or equivalent (e) Pressure SIMV, with pressure support (f) Volume SIMV, with pressure support (g) Pressure Support Ventilation with selectable volume and pressure mo des for apnea back-up (h) Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Mode. 2. Basic Setting capabilities (a) Tidal Volume 20mL- 1500 mL (b) Flow pattern: square wave and decelerating selection in VCV (c) Mandatory respiratory rate -5-80 breaths per minute (d) Inspiratory time-10 to 80% of breath cycle time (e) Inspiratory plateau 0 to 60% of inspiratory time (f) Rise time-0 to 20% of inspiratory time (g) PEEP 0 to 40 cm H20 (h) PS/PC above PEEP-0 to 50 cm H2O (i) FiO2-21 to 100 % (j) End expiration (% of peak flow) : 1-70 (k) Triggering-Both Flow and Pressure trigger must be available (l) Peak flow :≥ 200 I/min 3. The ventilator should have a dedicated mode for non-invasive ventilation (NI V). The following modes must be available with NIV a. CPAP b. Bi-level positive airway pressure (BiPAP) 4. There must be options for leak compensation and tube resistance compensati on. 5. A reliable and dedicated automated method of PEEP titration and lung protec tive ventilation for ARDS must be available, e.g., Open Lung tool, P/V Pro etc. 6. The I:E ratios must be easily changeable. The ventilator must be capable of d elivering I:E ratios of 1:6- 4:1 or better. 7. It must be capable of both flow and pressure triggering. The flow trigger sensi tivity range must be 0.5 L/min - 10L/min or better. The pressure triggering rang e must be - 10cm H2O- 0cm H2O or better. 8. The cycling threshold in NIV and rise time in invasive ventilation modes must

be user adjustable. It is preferable if the times are actual times/percentages an d not arbitrary levels. 9. The time interval before apnea backup ventilation is triggered (in spontaneou s modes of ventilation like PSV and NIV) must be user-settable. MONITORING AND CONTROL 1. The following must be monitored by the ventilator and displayed as needed. a. Peak airway pressure b. Plateau airway pressure c. Mean airway pressure d. Inspired Tidal Volume e. Expired tidal volume f. Minute Volume g. Static Compliance h. Dynamic Compliance i. Resistance- Inspired and expired j. Respiratory Rate (set) k. Respiratory Rate (total) l. PEEP m. Auto-PEEP n. RSBI o. Work of breathing p. P 0.1 q. Oxygen Inlet Pressure r. Air Inlet Pressure s. FiO2 (measured) t. Delivered FiO2 (set) u. Leak amount v. Time constant w. Elastance 2. It must be capable of performing standard manoeuvres like: a. Inspiratory Hold b. Expiratory Hold c. One-touch increase in FiO2 to 1.0 for suctioning

d. One touch standby and wake-up e. One-touch nebulisation control 3. The ventilator must be capable of: a. Must be able to connect and operate the Aerogen vibrating mesh plate nebuliser with a module built into the ventilator. Each ventilator must be s upplied with two autoclavable Aerogen Pro delivery sets (one installed an d one spare). 4. Oxygen sensors : It is preferable if the ventilator has permanent oxygen sens ors. a. If a disposable oxygen sensor is used, it should be replaced by the com pany during the warranty and CAMC period. 5. Flow sensors: a. For disposable proximal flow sensors, fifty sensors per ventilator must be provided at the time of purchase, and ten sensors per ventilator per ye ar must be provided by the company for the warranty period. b. For reusable distal flow sensors, ten sensors per ventilator must be prov ided at the time of purchase. Five additional sensors per year per ventilato r must be provided by the company throughout the warranty period. 6. The system should have a single-unit reusable, autoclavable expiratory valve/ cassette for complete disinfection. ALARMS 1. The following alarms must be standard. Limits must be user adjustable: a. Airway pressure b. Expired minute volume c. No patient effort (apnea) alarm with automatic return to support mode o n patient triggering d. No consistent patient effort e. Respiratory frequency f. End-expiratory pressure g. High continuous pressure

h. Oxygen Concentration i. Gas supply pressure j. Battery-low charge, low battery voltage k. EtCO2 Limits l. Leakage out of range in NIV m. Technical alarms ( Specific technical faults in internal circuitry) 2. The nature and cause of the alarm must be clearly displayed on the screen. DISPLAY 1. It should be at least 12 inches in size and a TFT/LED touchscreen display. Du al touchscreen and wheel controls are preferable. 2. It must be capable of displaying at least 3 scalars and 2 loops simultaneously for each breath, and a 24-hour trend display of measured parameters. 3. It must preferably display how changing settings influence the breath wavefo rm. 4. The display brightness must be adjustable, and must be readable in bright su nlight. 5. Commonly changed parameters of a breath- The control variable, limit variab le, cycle variable and baseline variable of a breath, Respiratory Rate and FiO2 must be changeable from the home display without using additional menus or o perations. 6. It must have a spill proof and easily cleanable screen display. 7. It should be provided with servo-controlled humidifier with all the accessories ) e.g., Thermostatically servo-controlled humidifier with temperature probe for d igital monitoring of the temperature with alarm facility, reusable heated wire ad apter suitable for disposable/ non-disposable circuit, heating chamber, mountin g brackets, power cord, facility to select active/passive humidification) for smoo th functioning.
